title: Decoded #10: Budget Season: Making the Case for Creative Spend to Finance
hook: Media gets approved in five minutes. Creative gets twenty minutes of questions. Here's why.
caption:
Media spend gets approved in five minutes. Creative spend gets twenty minutes of questions.

The reason is simple: finance funds what it can measure, and creative usually arrives without a measure.

In Issue #9 of Decoded, Raj and Sunil show how to make the case for creative in the language finance already uses: cost per order by attribute, spend that taught you nothing, and time to a new winner. Plus a five-step plan to ask for a learning budget instead of a production budget, ahead of the new financial year.

newsletter.draft_markdown:
# Decoded · Issue #9 — Budget season: making the case for creative spend to finance
*Skeleton — Raj to write in full, with Sunil reviewing the finance framing. ~1,500 words when finished. Sends Wed 27 Jan (moved from Tue 26 for Republic Day), just before the Union Budget (expected 1 Feb) and FY-end planning.*

**Opening (Monday, 9:40 a.m.):** Sam presents next year's plan to the CFO. Media spend gets approved in five minutes. Creative production gets twenty minutes of questions: "Why do we need more ads? Didn't we make 200 last year?"

**Key takeaways (draft):**
1. Finance funds what it can measure. Creative spend usually arrives without a measure.
2. Price the attribute, not the ad: show what a winning hook or proof moment was worth in cost per order.
3. Ask for a learning budget with a fixed test share, and report back on what it taught.

**Section 1 — Why creative loses the budget argument.** Media has a dashboard; creative has a mood board. "We need more content" isn't a business case.

**Section 2 — Three numbers finance understands.** Cost per order by attribute; spend wasted on ads that taught nothing; time to a new winner. Use anonymised galvor.ai results as illustrations only: beauty D2C +112% RoAS and 30% less wasted spend; fashion D2C $3,800 reallocated in month one; wellness D2C 2.6× uplift vs aspirational content. Always say "anonymised client".

**Section 3 — Building the case, step by step.** (1) Audit last year: how many ads, how many taught you something? (2) Put a number on repeated mistakes. (3) Propose a test budget with questions attached (Issue #7's test calendar). (4) Agree a review rhythm with finance (Issue #8's loop). (5) Report learnings quarterly, in rupees.

**Section 4 — What Galvor saw in the data.** [DATA NEEDED: share of annual creative spend, across brands we work with, that went to look-alike variants (anonymised) — ties to 48% less spend for 6+ look-alikes in three days.]

**Section 5 — The shift for marketers and leaders: five moves.** (1) Bring finance one page, not a deck. (2) Talk in cost per order, not views. (3) Separate the production budget from the learning budget. (4) Promise answers, not volume. (5) Invite finance to one review meeting a quarter.

**Close:** "Media got optimised to the decimal. The content running through it didn't." Budget season is when that gap gets funded, or doesn't.

**Next issue:** TBC — decide at the 1 Feb huddle (options: regional-language creative; creators vs brand-led ads).
